name: Analenzor User Behavior Analytics
author: analenzor

sections.description:
Analenzor connects your WordPress website to the Analenzor service for user behavior analytics and session replay. Explore visitor interactions and recordings in the external Analenzor dashboard.

Version 1.0.10 introduces a redesigned, responsive administration screen, improved tracking configuration, safer script data encoding, and isolated admin styles.

آنالنزور وب‌سایت وردپرسی شما را به سرویس تحلیل رفتار کاربران و بازپخش نشست‌های آنالنزور متصل می‌کند. نسخه 1.0.10 دارای رابط تنظیمات جدید، پشتیبانی از نمایش راست‌به‌چپ و بهبودهای فنی در بارگذاری اسکریپت است. گزارش‌ها در داشبورد آنالنزور نمایش داده می‌شوند، نه در پیشخوان وردپرس.

Features:

  • Configure your tracking ID and enable or disable tracking.
  • Load the external tracking script asynchronously.
  • Open the Analenzor dashboard directly from the settings screen.
  • Responsive administration interface with Persian and English copy.
  • No analytics requests are initiated by this plugin until tracking is enabled and a tracking ID is saved.

An Analenzor account and a configured website in the service are required. Service availability and features depend on your Analenzor account.

External Services

This plugin integrates with the external Analenzor service, provided by Analenzor.

When the site owner enables tracking and saves a non-empty tracking ID, public website pages load JavaScript from:
https://dashboard.analenzor.com/api/script/

The request includes the configured website tracking ID and an hourly cache version. Loading the script makes a request from the visitor’s browser to Analenzor, exposing ordinary network request information such as the visitor’s IP address and browser headers to that service. The remote script supplies behavior analytics and session replay functionality and may collect interactions, page information, and session data according to the service configuration and privacy policy. The remote script is not bundled with this plugin.

For signed-in visitors, the plugin also makes the WordPress username and first assigned role available to the remote script through the JavaScript variable window.analenzor_custom_user. Do not treat tracked signed-in sessions as necessarily anonymous.

The plugin does not include a consent banner or automatic integration with consent-management plugins. Site owners are responsible for providing appropriate disclosures and obtaining consent where required before enabling tracking. Disabling tracking stops this plugin from inserting its script on subsequent uncached page loads; clear page caches after changing tracking settings.

Dashboard: https://dashboard.analenzor.com
Terms of Service: https://dashboard.analenzor.com/terms
Privacy Policy: https://dashboard.analenzor.com/privacy
sections.installation:
1. Upload the analenzor-user-behavior-analytics folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the plugin through WordPress.
  2. Activate the plugin from the Plugins screen.
  3. Open Analenzor in the WordPress administration menu.
  4. Enter the tracking ID from your Analenzor website settings. Enter only the ID, not a URL or script.
  5. Review your privacy and consent requirements, enable tracking, and save settings.
  6. Clear any page cache and visit the public website. Review reports in your Analenzor dashboard.
sections.faq:
Does the settings page verify the connection?

No. The status indicates whether tracking is enabled with a saved ID. It is not a successful connectivity test or confirmation that data has arrived.

Where can I view reports?

In the external Analenzor dashboard. This plugin does not display live analytics inside WordPress.

Why do I not see sessions?

Check the tracking ID, saved enable switch, page cache, browser blockers, consent requirements, content security policy, and service availability. Processing time is controlled by Analenzor.

Has this release been tested on the latest WordPress?

Latest-version runtime compatibility has not yet been verified for this release candidate. The Tested up to field retains the previous package’s value and does not represent a new test. Complete staging tests before publishing and update the field only to a version actually tested.
sections.changelog:
1.0.10

  • Redesigned the settings interface with responsive cards, accessible controls, and RTL support.
  • Added working dashboard links and configuration status without implying verified connectivity.
  • Limited administration styles to the plugin settings page.
  • Corrected the bundled font path.
  • Moved tracking registration to the standard frontend script enqueue hook.
  • Replaced incorrect scalar wp_localize_script usage with JSON-encoded inline data.
  • Safely handled signed-in users without an assigned role.
  • Stopped loading signed-in user integration when tracking is disabled or unconfigured.
  • Improved tracking ID input handling, attribute escaping, and script URL encoding.
  • Preserved existing option names and documented external service and identity data handling.

1.0.0

  • Initial release with session replay and interaction tracking.
